**Implementation Plan: Playable Minecraft-like Game in Go (Ebitengine V2)**

Architecture overview:
- A single Go binary using Ebitengine v2 for rendering, input, and game loop
- Chunk-based voxel world (16×64×16 chunks) with Perlin noise terrain generation
- First-person camera (mouse look + WASD, space to jump, shift to descend)
- Block types: air, grass, dirt, stone, sand, wood, leaves, water, planks, cobblestone
- Ray-casting for block interaction (left click = remove, right click = place)
- Simple sky rendering with color gradient
- Minimal UI: crosshair + hotbar at bottom showing selected block type

File breakdown:
```
/tmp/mcgo/
├── go.mod
├── main.go              — entry point, Ebitengine game loop
├── world/
│   ├── chunk.go          — chunk struct (16×64×16 blocks), ChunkPos
│   ├── world.go          — World struct: map[ChunkPos]*Chunk, generation, Get/Set
│   └── generator.go      — Perlin noise terrain heightmap generator
├── block/
│   └── block.go          — BlockType enum, block properties (solid, transparent, color)
├── player/
│   ├── player.go         — Position, Velocity, Yaw, Pitch, movement update
│   └── interaction.go    — Ray-cast for block pick/place (DDA algorithm)
├── render/
│   └── render.go         — Batch mesh building per chunk, sorting, drawing
└── camera/
    └── camera.go         — View/projection matrix from player state
```

**Plan: Create a playable Minecraft-like voxel game in Go using Ebitengine v2, inside `/tmp/mcgo`.**

Architecture overview:
- Ebitengine v2 for rendering, input, and game loop
- Chunk-based voxel world (16×64×16 chunks) with Perlin noise terrain generation
- First-person camera: mouse look + WASD movement, space to jump, shift to descend
- Block types: air, grass, dirt, stone, sand, wood, leaves, water, planks, cobblestone
- Ray-casting (DDA) for block interaction: left click = remove, right click = place
- Sky rendered as color gradient
- Minimal UI: crosshair + hotbar at bottom showing selected block type
- Separate Go module at `/tmp/mcgo` (not modifying the existing agent codebase)

File structure:
```
/tmp/mcgo/
├── go.mod
├── main.go               — entry point, Ebitengine game loop
├── world/
│   ├── chunk.go          — chunk struct (16×64×16 blocks), ChunkPos, mesh caching
│   ├── world.go          — World struct with map[ChunkPos]*Chunk, Get/Set, loading
│   └── generator.go      — Perlin noise terrain generator
├── block/
│   └── block.go          — BlockType enum, properties (solid, transparent, color)
├── player/
│   ├── player.go         — Position, Velocity, Yaw, Pitch, movement update
│   └── interaction.go    — Ray-cast (DDA) for block pick/place
├── render/
│   └── render.go         — Chunk mesh building, face culling, draw call batching
└── camera/
    └── camera.go         — View and projection matrix from player state
```

Implementation order:
1. go.mod and main.go — empty game window with Ebitengine
2. block/block.go — block type definitions and properties
3. world/generator.go — Perlin noise height function
4. world/chunk.go — chunk data structure
5. world/world.go — world map with chunk generation
6. camera/camera.go — 3D view/projection matrices
7. player/player.go — movement and physics
8. player/interaction.go — ray-cast block picking
9. render/render.go — chunk mesh building and rendering
10. main.go integration — full game loop with input handling

Success criteria:
- Window opens with a generated 3D terrain
- Player can move with WASD, look around with mouse
- Left click removes a block, right click places a block from hotbar
- Hotbar shows 9 block types, scroll wheel selects
- Terrain has hills, valleys, grass/dirt/stone layers
- FPS stays above 30 on a reasonable machine
- Chunks only rebuild mesh when blocks change (not every frame)

END_STEP
